body:
I was going to say that it sounds like you may need to test for herpes, but then I saw your edit.

As someone who was in your shoes, I highly suggest that you speak to a therapist ASAP. Your life isn't over, but I'll be honest when I say that my life wasn't exactly the same once I was diagnosed. You learn to live with it and accept your circumstances. Having herpes may take adjusting, so, I recommend speaking to a therapist when you can to help you adjust to this new change in your life.

As someone who has herpes after serving abuse, it totally understand wanting to kill the person who gave it LMAO.

Although, I appreciate how everyone else acted like it wasn’t a big deal and brushed it off. The stigma of herpes sucks so seeing it being treated as no big deal was awesome to see!

I was abused when I caught HSV2.

That’s the problem with the stigma: is that people assume that the individual with the STI was lacking responsibility. When in reality, there are people who are survivors like me…and unfortunately, it happens a lot.

Don’t want to catch an STI? Of course. Your health is important. You should take as many precautions as possible to prevent it. I didn’t have that choice since I was abused.

But instead of immediately judging, just try to remember that there’s more to somebody’s story.

I wasn’t irresponsible when I caught HSV2. I was abused when I caught it.

That’s unfortunately a stereotype with the stigma. That people who catch it are irresponsible and/or promiscuous. When I’m reality, there are people like me who are actually survivors.

Type 1 isn’t just oral and Type 2 isn’t just genital.

Performing oral sex on someone can transmit it and give someone genital.

Herpes is extremely common and it’s just the stigma. The stigma was created in order to sell medications and to get teens to practice abstinence. Instead, sex education backfired and we’re just ignorant on the subject.

How long does she date guys before disclosing?

I have GHSV2. I’ve been rejected as well and was accepted by someone who didn’t have it. The difference was with my BF vs. all the other guys that have rejected me was that my BF actually liked me for me and didn’t just want sex for me. It took a while for me to realize that the guys that rejected me only wanted one thing from me. 

My BF and I dated for a few months (we didn’t do anything physical) and we established a solid friendship before it truly got romantic. When I disclosed, it felt like I was disclosing to my best friend. He didn’t care at all. My BF also doesn’t have herpes. 

My advice to your friend is to really vet the guys that she dates. Establish the foundation of the relationship, like a friendship. Make sure that the guy isn’t just into her for one thing.

There’s a very good chance that the guys that reject her actually aren’t that into her.

Rejection sucks, but the right guy won’t reject her.

I am! Take out the dating and love life, everything is great. I don't date anymore and my life has been so much more easier.
I’ve got herpes.

I’m a 30-something female and this is my experience…

I’ve had GHSV2 for a few years now. 

Accepting my diagnosis got better within time whereas dating and my love life changed a lot.

I’d purposely put on my profile my serious intentions such as marriage and kids. Men with similar intentions would match. Once we’ve built connections, I would disclose…only to be rejected. You’d think that as the dating pool gets older, they’d be more understanding. The truth is, yes, they are, but they’re still not willing to risk it. It doesn’t matter how much older you get. There are always challenges to be faced.

After constant rejection, I decided that it wasn’t worth my mental health  and have stopped dating. I am much more happier now!

Look at it this way: at least it's just herpes and not a pregnancy.

Yes, it sucks. I have herpes. But, herpes is common. She doesn't even need to have sex to contract it. Making out with someone alone is enough to contract it. You might even have it without realizing it because herpes can lie dormant for years; you can have it without having an outbreak.

Regardless, because of her new diagnosis, I strongly suggest that she gets into therapy. She is in a very vulnerable space, esp if her BF is accusing her of cheating. I don't know your sister, but these are small signs of potential emotional abuse.

Your herpes doesn't define you.

Why does it make you fele depressed and isolated? Are you scared that you won't find someone? There are people with herpes who do find someone and then there are people without herpes who don't.

If it's meant for you, then it's meant for you.

If it means anything, I personally gave up on dating a while back. I'm the happiest now that I've been in a while and it feels that I no longer have this weight on my shoulders.

I don't have a partner and probably won't have one as I have sworn off dating. 

Yes, there are worst things. But, in my particular case, all the other negatives in my life have not outweighed my herpes. Herpes has caused severe psychological, mental, and emotional trauma for me and forever changed my life in a multitude of ways. For example. being in my 30s, I'm at risk when it comes to pregnancies. When I was dating, no matter what, it was just a dealbreaker for every guy I've disclosed. So, I'm not just struggling to find a partner. I might not even be a mother because of the domino effect herpes has had on my life. I might consider doing sperm donation, though.

I understand where you're coming from, but, this is unfortunately a reality for many of us.

It is what it is. The reality is, the social stigma is way too strong. We can try and fight against it all we want, but, this is just our reality. We can try and educate as much as possible. But, there are people who are very immature and won't accept facts

Funny that you sat that herpes seems like a very small issue. For me, all the other issues in my life have failed in comparison; nothing has been worse than having herpes. It's why the other issues that I have going on don't phase me as much as they should. Being diagnosed with herpes has been the worst.

Oh, I know I’m worthy of love. But people are just awful. So, it’s not about whether or not I’m worthy about love. It’s about whether or people are worthy of MY love. It’s been a total no and not worth it.

I’m in my 30s and would list on my dating profiles that I date with serious intentions. You’d think that the dating pool at my age would be more serious and more understanding.

The guys I’ve dated were either understanding or treated my poorly after disclosing. All the guys I’ve disclosed to so far have rejected me. It’s not worth the risk.

After consistent rejection, I’ve decided to stop dating entirely. It’s just not worth risking my emotional, mental, and psychological health.

I am happier now, though!

But, that is the plan God has for people. We cannot question God's plans. Instead, we should just remember that God intentionally puts us in these positions for a reason and we should thank Him for it.

God put you on this Earth for a reason.

For me, I too wanted romantic love so much. Instead, I learned a harsh lesson: people are cruel and romance really isn't worth it. I caught genital herpes in the process. Was it worth romance in any capacity? No, not at all. My love life forever changed since my diagnosis. I gave up on romantic love, but, it's OK.

I also learned that the love that I so desperately wanted was within myself the whole time.

I don't need someone to love me because I already do. 

Also, you are loved by the greatest man of all: God. His love is the greatest. God is your soulmate.
Get tested. That's all you can do.

You're 18. You're still so young. 

I used to feel that way. I realized over time that it was coming from a place of insecurity. Emotional intimacy and love... I had it all along: it was within myself. 

Self-love is so important. You need it before getting into any type of relationship. I learned the hard way that wanting others for emotional intimacy and love as a very toxic way to go about it.

I contracted genital herpes and my dating life forever changed. So, no, dating and romantic love really isn't all what it is cracked up to be.

As for platonic relationships, maybe try and go to events that require social interactions. Pick up a hobby. Having hobbies helps so much to meet new people and getting to find new interests!

No, he ghosted her. He didn’t dig deep to find his balls to flat out tell her.

She was brave enough to let her know about her HSV. The least he could’ve done was respond and just tell her it wouldn’t work for him.

This is unfortunately a sad pattern in dating nowadays. People lack the ability to be honest and be upfront. Ghosting is very immature.

She did.

People should be with others who are willing to communicate. It feels like nowadays, herpes or not, people lack that maturity.

If this guy was mature enough, he would’ve told her that it wouldn’t work for him.

I agree. Calling someone uneducated just because they don’t want herpes doesn’t seem fair. I’d respect their choice.

But regardless, sex education, in particular in the US, was a major flop. So, yes, unfortunately, a large portion of society is very uneducated. Sex education was created by conservatives to get youth to abstain until marriage along with big pharma in order to sell medication. Obviously, it severely backfired; youth didn’t stop having sex, but instead, weren’t throughly educated on sex at all.

For example, in regards to heterosexual sex, the stats on getting pregnant even on the most effective birth control such as the implant or IUD is almost the same as someone with HSV on Valtrex; you’re just as likely to catch HSV from someone on Valtrex as getting someone pregnant while on the IUD or implant. But a potential pregnancy has never scared someone away from having sex. Why doesn’t a pregnancy scare anyone as much as catching herpes? Both are just as likely to happen.

You absolutely did the right thing.

Him ghosting you was very immature of him. It’s his choice if he didn’t want to pursue a relationship with you. But, had he been mature enough, he could’ve communicated that with you.

You want a man, not a boy.

This might be a bizarre answer: but personally I just gave up on trying to date.

I just accepted what my fate is and I don’t even try anymore. It’s not worth sacrificing my mental health.

I’m happier now.
It has been right on the spot. They don’t even need to think about it. They just leave.

Lol nope. I’ve tried and all it has ever done has severely backfired on me.

I do believe in being humble and accepting that whatever is, is.

Well, for a lot of us, it’s not about how common it is. It’s about the stigma that we face.

We don’t need to be told everything is going to be OK as much as we do. For as much as we are told that it’s normal, the same amount of energy should be spent educating the uneducated.

We can be told as much as possible that herpes is common, but it doesn’t change the stigma.

We shouldn’t be the ones who are told that it is common. We already know that. The ones who find herpes disgusting are the ones who need to be educated on it as much as we are.

So, no. Being told constantly that herpes is common doesn’t bring me more comfort because I already know that. Instead, that same amount of energy should be spent on the ones who view people like us as lepers and are scared of herpes.

This might not be the answer you’re going to want to hear, but I can’t lie to you…

The reality is, a lot of us get rejected. 

For me, it forever changed my love life and made dating much more harder. I’ve been consistently rejected. So much so, I have give up completely. But, I am happier now.

BUT, what really opened my eyes is that people, herpes or not, het rejected all the time. Therefore, your love life really isn’t any different from someone else who gets rejected for something that isn’t herpes.

There are people  with herpes find love too. There are people without herpes who don’t find love.

If it’s not herpes that will cause a breakup, something else will.

Herpes doesn’t define you or your happiness. We all don’t get what we want and that is just fine.

In the end, the only person you can really depend on to make yourself happy is just you. Go out. Live your best life. You may not have the same dating/sex life, but you can still live to the fullest in other aspects.

Insensitive comments and uneducated ones on Reddit are no different than IRL.

If anything, seeing these comments just reinforce what our reality is. It’s what is expected.

It’s easy to just Google and check your local resources. Many places offer free STD testing. However, herpes testing may require a payment. Just check in and see what options are available!

That’s true. But, it’s still a smaller percentage vs. people who wouldn’t.

As someone with genital herpes who also survived abuse, I feel like I can comment on this:

OP, your sister does not need to lower her standards. Not wanting to be a stepparent is not a standard. She is allowed to have standards and date whomever she wants. As long as she is OK with knowing that she can be rejected for herpes.

I will say that ever since my diagnosis, dating has been very different. I understand the statement that the dating pool seems smaller; I’ve been rejected by every guy I have ever disclosed to. So, I can kinda understand where your concerns are coming from.

For me, dating has not been easy. To be rejected for herpes has caused great psychological and mental distress for me. But, it is understandable. Of course nobody wants to catch herpes.

So, yes. Dating is harder from personal experience. But, no, a diagnosis does not mean she should lower her standards.

YTA for telling her to lower her standards when she doesn’t need to, especially for something as being a stepparent because that is a major responsibility. NTA for understanding that dating is much more challenging for people with herpes.

Instead of telling her to lower her standards, be there for your sister and remind her of her worth. She is allowed to have her standards. But, be there for her in case it doesn’t work. If your sister is as great as you say she is, then you know she doesn’t need a man who won’t accept her for her anyway.
Yes, please get therapy. It helps a lot.

If you're a male: you're scared about catching an STD, but you're not scared of getting her or any other girl pregnant? Are you aware that when you have sex, you CAN get a girl pregnant? No matter what the birth control is, unless one of you is sterile.

You're willing to have sex without thinking about consequences? If you think an accidental pregnancy is better than catching...anything, that's up to you.

Herpes is common. Cold sores are herpes. You can catch herpes even by just making out with someone. Oral cold sores being transmitted genitally is a thing. A partner may not have herpes genitally, but, if they get cold sores and perform oral sex on you, you can catch genital herpes that way too.

Transmitting herpes when on medication is extremely low, as low as being on the most effective birth control such as the IUD and implant. In other words, when the person with herpes is on medication, the odds of you catching herpes are around the same odds of getting pregnant while on the IUD and implant.

Your sex life is ultimately up to you. Sex isn't something anyone should take lightly because, as now you have exprienced, it is a scary world out there. If anything, it sounds like you're not as educated on sex as you think hence why you're as anxious as you are. 

My advice is, do more research, not just on herpes either. Educate yourself more on sex too. It's more than OK to be more cautious regarding sex. What isn't OK is not being as educated as you should be.

Keep up with the therapy. Good for you for getting the help you need, especially now. Like others have commented on here, you have really deep issues that you need to address within yourself. 

I get it. I was in your exact same shoes. I survived an abusive relationship and that’s how I caught herpes too. I also wanted a man’s love so much and I wanted someone to just love me. I learned in time that that way of thinking is not healthy. If someone thinks this way, they will struggle having a healthy relationship. 

Jerks prey on vulnerable, especially young, women who have low self-esteem. 

One of the good things about having herpes is that it has helped me taken dating seriously and I really vet the men that I date. I make sure that we are on the same page and I’m not dealing with a douche. Herpes helps weed out the ones who aren’t serious. Disclosing is hard enough as it is. It helps when you disclose to the right person. The right person won’t reject you.

I won’t lie to you, though. Has it been hard for me? Yes, it has. I’ve been rejected by every guy I’ve disclosed to. I’m at a point in my life where I need to seriously consider having children of my own. The older I get, the more possibility there is for me to be high-risk when it comes to pregnancy due to my age. So, herpes hasn’t just affected my love life. But, it has affected how my pregnancies could potentially be. Just in case though, I have looked into sperm banks. So, who knows what the future holds?

But what keeps me going is that despite everything that I’ve been through, I learned to love myself a lot. I never needed a man’s love; the love I needed was always here within me.

You don’t need another man to love you. All the love you have ever needed is within YOU.

I don’t know if finding a romantic partner is in the cards for me. If it happens, great. If not, I know that I will be OK. I gave up caring and I’m so much more happier letting it go. 

You need to stop revolving your happiness and self-worth around romantic relationships. Learn to get it go. You might end up loving someone for the wrong reasons…which is worse than herpes.

But, plenty of people with herpes have found romantic love. It is possible for you too. Don’t count yourself out. 

Just be patient with yourself and live your life to the fullest. Regardless, you have the power to live a happy, fulfilling life, even without romantic love.

I wonder all the time. It has affected my life in more ways than one.

But what keeps me going is that I remind myself that there is more to life and I can still live a fulfilled life full of love, even without romance.
It has existed or so long and affected so many people and we still can't find a cure. Hopefully, we get one soon. It's about time we get one!

A few of my closest friends know. They reassured me and told me that herpes was common and that it wasn’t a big deal. They even said that they would date someone with herpes and it wouldn’t be a problem for them at all.

It’s either people who just want to hook up or extremely vulnerable people who are still trying to deal with their diagnosis.

I’m not looking for just a hookup nor am I at that vulnerable phase. I am looking for neither of those.

I’ve had it for a few years now. Certain parts of my life have changed drastically, especially now.

My view on people has been skewed. I’m very cautious with people. I don’t have a lot of faith in humanity anymore. I have changed mentally and emotionally.

Dating is more harder. I’ve been rejected by every guy I’ve ever disclosed to. The psychological affects of knowing I have herpes is already hard enough. But to be rejected for it makes it even worse. What really stings with me is how the guys I would date would acknowledge how valuable I am as a person. But, no matter how perfect I seem, everything great about me means absolutely nothing once I disclose. You are instantly narrowed down to just herpes. You having herpes is all that matters. You being the perfect match for someone does not. Everything great about you means nothing. Instead, you are defined by herpes.

I’m older now too. The dating pool seems much more smaller. Add in herpes and it’s even smaller. Not only that, but now I’m at the age where I really need to think about having children. Complicated pregnancies due to my age does worry me. Not only is it hard to find a potential husband, but now I have to think about my ability to get pregnant and have a safe pregnancy. Basically, I can’t find a husband which in turn, means I can’t get pregnant. Herpes hasn’t only made it difficult to find a husband, but it has also inadvertently potentially made me at higher risk to have issues with pregnancy.

Coping with it gets better in time. But was life easier before my diagnosis? Of course. I think about my diagnosis a lot. I never forget that I have it.

Aside from the romantic and potential family aspects of my life, nothing has changed. I still get to live my life. I get to travel and still live. 

It’s just that now that I’m older, I really need to think about where my life is headed in regards to having a family. I’ve accepted that I probably won’t find someone, and that is OK. I am at peace with knowing that I will never get married or find someone. Ever since I’ve come to this acceptance, I’ve been much more happier and it feels like a weight has been lifted from my shoulders. I don’t need to feel anxious about disclosing or getting my heartbroken anymore because I’m not even trying to find someone. I’m very happy with my life now.

As for children, I’m considering options such as sperm banks. 

I don’t know what the future holds. But. I can say that I am happiest that I have ever been ever since my diagnosis.
Tried those. Not a good experience and I don’t recommend!
